Coordinates u=b−c,v=a−b,w=b+c−a>0 yield an exact nonnegative quadratic identity q²−(u+dv+rw)²=2(1−r)uw+(2/3)(2−η−r)v[2u+(2−η+d)v+(2−η)w], r=sqrt(1−η+η²), d=(2−η+2r)/3. Thus R≥fP+κ(a−c), f=(1+η+r)/3, κ=2(1−f), strict for non-equilateral triangles. Known fixed-triangle theorem proves equality at equilateral. Perimeter monotonicity and (1,1,ε) degeneration prove κ best possible, and compact cone zero-locus proves unique degeneration. Independent SymPy identity and sampled positive-cone computations support the nonnegative remainder proof.
